title: First-order line-section obstruction and its Serre-dual multiplication formula
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective], and let $L$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Set $A=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ [def-sc-dual-numbers], $C_A=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $L_A$ be an invertible module on $C_A$ with a fixed identification $L_A/\epsilon L_A\simeq L$. If $t_{ij}$ are transition functions of $L$ and the transitions of $L_A$ are $t_{ij}(1+\epsilon a_{ij})$, let $v=[a_{ij}]\in H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$; the cohomology is ordinary Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Write $\partial_v:H^0(C,L)\to H^1(C,L)$ for the boundary of $0\to L\xrightarrow{\epsilon}L_A\to L\to0$. Then $\partial_v(s)$ is the class of the Cech cocycle $a_{ij}s_j$, interpreted using the transition functions of $L$. With $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ [def-sc-kahler-differentials] $L^{-1}:=L^{\vee}$ [def-sc-invertible-module], and the Serre trace pairings $\langle-,-\rangle_{\mathcal M}:H^1(C,\mathcal M)\otimes_kH^0(C,\mathcal M^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C)\to k$ of [det-thm-picard-duality] (cup product, evaluation, then the residue trace $t_C$) for $\mathcal M=\mathcal O_C$ and $\mathcal M=L$, one has
$$\langle\partial_v(s),t\rangle_L=\langle v,s t\rangle_{\mathcal O_C}\quad\text{for }t\in H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes L^{-1}).$$
A simultaneous opposite convention for the boundary and Cech differential changes both sides by the same sign. More precisely, if $R\Gamma(C_A,L_A)$ in the derived category [def-pc-derived-category] is represented by a two-term finite free $A$-complex $[E_A^0\xrightarrow{d_A}E_A^1]$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], with reduction $[E^0\xrightarrow{d_0}E^1]$, the map $\ker d_0\to\operatorname{coker}d_0$ sending $x$ to the class of $\epsilon^{-1}d_A(\widetilde x)$ is $\partial_v$ under the natural cohomology identifications. Here $\widetilde x$ is any lift, and $\epsilon E_A^1$ is identified with $E^1$; this is independent of the lift and the complex model.

source.place: Tag 0C6R (lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening), split dual-number case; curves.tex Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1) and 0BS4 (remark-rework-duality-locally-free) for natural Serre duality. The section-boundary and two-term-model formulas are an agent expansion, not an assertion that 0C6R states them verbatim.

proof.text: Use the split projection $p:C_A\to C$. The spaces $C_A$ and $C$ have the same opens: on $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, every prime of $R[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$ contains $\epsilon$, and basic opens correspond under reduction. On this space $\mathcal O_{C_A}=\mathcal O_C\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O_C$. Thus restriction of scalars $p_*$ on modules is exact; its left adjoint $p^*$ is exact as well, being extension by this free rank-two algebra. By [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], $p_*$ preserves injectives. An injective resolution on $C_A$ therefore also computes derived global sections after restriction to $C$, with the same sections and differentials. This identifies the derived sections and the boundaries, not only their dimensions. Locally $L_A$ is free of rank one, and reduction gives the exact sequence $0\to L\xrightarrow{\iota}p_*L_A\to L\to0$, where $\iota(u)=\epsilon\widetilde u$ for any lift. It is well-defined since two lifts differ by $\epsilon L_A$ and $\epsilon^2=0$; its image is precisely the kernel of reduction.

source.place: Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0C6R, split thickening, with the displayed affine calculation

proof.text: Fix the transition convention $e_j=t_{ij}e_i$ for frames of $L$ and $e_{A,j}=t_{ij}(1+\epsilon a_{ij})e_{A,i}$ for the chosen lifts. Write $s=s_i e_i=s_j e_j$, so $s_i=t_{ij}s_j$, and choose $\widetilde s_i=s_i e_{A,i}$. On an overlap $\widetilde s_j-\widetilde s_i=\epsilon t_{ij}a_{ij}s_j e_{A,i}$. Under $\iota^{-1}$ this is $a_{ij}s_i e_i=a_{ij}s_j e_j$. The triple-overlap equation for the transitions gives $a_{ik}=a_{ij}+a_{jk}$, since $\epsilon^2=0$. Consequently these differences are precisely the image of the additive cocycle $(a_{ij})$ under the sheaf map $m_s:\mathcal O_C\to L$, $u\mapsto us$.

source.place: Tag 0C6R, lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening, proof: units 1+f; explicit transition calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-boundary-cech-compatibility] to the exact sequence of step 1 and its local lifts from step 2. Its sign is lift on $U_j$ minus lift on $U_i$. It identifies the image of $(a_{ij}s_j)$ under the canonical Cech comparison with $\partial_v(s)$. By [lem-sc-cech-h1-map-natural], applying $m_s$ to the cocycle and then comparing equals first comparing and applying $H^1(m_s)$. Since $v$ is the comparison image of $(a_{ij})$, we obtain $\partial_v(s)=H^1(m_s)(v)$. No claim that the chosen cover computes all cohomology is required.

source.place: Tag 01EQ, lemma-cech-cohomology, canonical natural comparison; Tag 0B8S, lemma-boundary-derivation-over-cup-product, local-lift calculation, with the sign convention fixed by the cited boundary node

proof.text: The curve $C$ is integral: its local rings are domains by [lem-sc-smooth-regular], so two irreducible components cannot meet (a common point would have a local ring with two minimal primes); $C$ is Noetherian, so its finitely many components are open and closed, and connectedness leaves one. It has dimension one by [def-sc-curves], and it is proper over $k$ by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Hence [det-thm-picard-duality] applies with $n=1$. Use its naturality clause with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_C$, $\mathcal G=L$, $q=1$, and $\varphi=m_s$; both are finite locally free. The dual map $m_s^{\vee}\otimes1:L^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C\to\mathcal O_C^{\vee}\otimes\omega_C=\omega_C$ sends $t$ to $st$: in the frame $e_i$, a dual section is $b_i e_i^{\vee}\otimes\eta_i$ and its image is $s_i b_i\eta_i$. Therefore $\langle\partial_v(s),t\rangle_L=\langle H^1(m_s)v,t\rangle_L=\langle v,st\rangle_{\mathcal O_C}$, for exactly the trace pairings of the statement. No comparison with another normalization of Serre duality is used.

source.place: Tag 0BS2, lemma-duality-dim-1, clause (5), and Tag 0BS4, remark-rework-duality-locally-free; naturality as explicitly stated in the latest blueprint det-thm-picard-duality

proof.text: Let $f:C_A\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $T$ be the canonical coefficient triangle $k\to A\to k\to k[1]$ in $D(A)$ of $0\to k\xrightarrow{1\mapsto\epsilon}A\to k\to0$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. On an affine trivializing open with ring $R\otimes_k A$, [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](2) gives $Lf^*\widetilde M\cong\widetilde{M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_A(R\otimes_kA)}$; as $R\otimes_kA$ is $A$-free (by a $k$-basis of $R$) there is no higher Tor, so $Lf^*\widetilde k=\mathcal O_C$ and $Lf^*\widetilde A=\mathcal O_{C_A}$, regarded as $\mathcal O_{C_A}$-modules. The line module $L_A$ is flat, so $L_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ of these is computed termwise: the three terms are $L$, $L_A$, $L$, and the first map is $r\mapsto\epsilon r$, exactly $\iota$. These identifications agree on overlaps. Thus $L_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*T$ is the canonical triangle of $0\to L\xrightarrow{\iota}L_A\to L\to0$; the exactness, signed shifts, and preservation of the connecting arrow for these derived tensor functors are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact].

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor, canonical exact tensor functor

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (it is projective, hence proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]), and $L_A$ is quasi-coherent. Apply [lem-pc-projection-formula] to $f$, $L_A[0]$, and the three coefficient objects $\widetilde k,\widetilde A,\widetilde k$ of $\widetilde T$, all of which have quasi-coherent cohomology. Its canonical maps are isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] these very maps, defined as counit mates, give a morphism of triangles including the connecting square, with the identity at the coefficient unit $A$. By [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh], $Rf_*L_A\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, so the triangulated equivalence of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] writes it as $\widetilde{K}$ with $K=R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*L_A)$, and [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](3) gives $\widetilde K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\widetilde M\cong\widetilde{K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AM}$. By [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition], $R\Gamma(Y,-)\circ Rf_*\cong R\Gamma(C_A,-)$. Applying $R\Gamma(Y,-)$ thus identifies $R\Gamma(C_A,L_A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AT$ with the derived-global-sections triangle of step 5. By the injective-resolution identification in step 1 and [def-sc-module-cohomology-boundary], its degree-zero boundary is exactly $\partial_v$, with end groups $H^0(C,L)$ and $H^1(C,L)$. In particular the identifications with the reduced model are the canonical ones from this coefficient triangle, rather than arbitrary vector-space isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08EU, lemma-cohomology-base-change; Tag 06Z0, lemma-affine-compare-bounded; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, its exact counit-mate construction

proof.text: Write $E_A=[E_A^0\xrightarrow{d_A}E_A^1]$ for the specified model and $E=E_A\otimes_Ak$. By [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], this bounded finite free complex is K-flat, so $E_A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AT$ is computed termwise, and by the signed-shift compatibility of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] it is the canonical triangle of the degreewise exact sequence $S_E:0\to E\xrightarrow{\epsilon}E_A\to E\to0$ of $A$-complexes; the first map sends $x$ to $\epsilon\widetilde x$ and the differential it induces on each end is $d_0$. Restriction of scalars to $k$ is exact; by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] it induces a functor on derived categories computed termwise. It sends the mapping cone of $S_E$, its quasi-isomorphism to $E$ and its projection to $E[1]$ to the same constructions for the underlying $k$-sequence, so it carries the canonical cone boundary of $S_E$ to that of the $k$-sequence, and it does not change cohomology. Over $k$ the sequence splits degreewise by the finite free bases, with section $x\mapsto\widetilde x$ and retraction $\epsilon\widetilde y\mapsto y$ on $\epsilon E_A$. By [lem-sc-p1-split-ses-boundary-comparison] the cone boundary is $Q$ of the chain map $\pi d_A s$. For $x\in\ker d_0$ with lift $\widetilde x$, $d_A(\widetilde x)\in\epsilon E_A^1$, so $H^0$ of this boundary sends $x$ to the class of $\epsilon^{-1}d_A(\widetilde x)$ in $\operatorname{coker}d_0$. By step 6 this is $\partial_v$; the end groups are $\ker d_0$ and $\operatorname{coker}d_0$ since the model is in degrees 0 and 1.

proof.text: If another lift is $\widetilde x+\epsilon z$, its image after division by $\epsilon$ differs by $d_0(\bar z)$, which is zero in the cokernel. For independence of the model, a specified derived isomorphism $E_A\simeq R\Gamma(C_A,L_A)$ induces, by functoriality of derived tensor, an isomorphism of its coefficient triangles, including their connecting arrows; the exact tensor and naturality assertions used in steps 5--7 are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The boundary is thus unchanged under the induced cohomology identifications, as required. Finally, the opposite simultaneous convention is obtained by negating the degree-one Cech-to-cohomology comparison and the boundary. It negates both $v$ and $\partial_v(s)$, so bilinearity negates the two sides of the pairing equality together; it does not assert that one can negate the boundary while fixing the convention for $v$.
